study_type: retrospective pre-tournament-information backtest; not contemporaneous predictions

figures.title: Separate selection from evaluation
figures.caption:
Ratings are frozen for validation and again for the tournament. The final refit includes validation history.
Retrospective reconstruction, not evidence of pre-event publication; current snapshot filtered by match date.

figures.title: The evidence behind the ratings
figures.caption:
Counts are eligible international matches, not unique teams. Training begins in 1990; no time weighting is applied.
2026 is a partial year ending 10 June. Annual volume is coverage, not a measure of predictive quality.

figures.title: How the leading teams reached the cutoff
figures.caption:
Eight tournament teams selected by their cutoff Elo rating, not by tournament results. Each line shows post-match-day ratings.
1500 initialization; simultaneous-day updates; constant K and home advantage selected on 2022–23 validation.

figures.title: The pre-tournament strength hierarchy
figures.caption:
Top 16 among the 48 tournament participants; this is not a ranking of every historical national side.
Ratings use matches strictly before 11 June 2026. Rating points are not title probabilities or uncertainty estimates.

figures.title: Selection over the complete parameter grid
figures.caption:
Every predeclared candidate is shown: 2 K values × 2 home advantages × 3 draw/scale values per family.
Cells are frozen-model 2022–23 validation log loss; lower is better. Orange outlines mark the selected candidate.

figures.title: Validation performance accumulates over time
figures.caption:
Cumulative mean loss over chronological validation matches, using fixed training-end ratings throughout.
These are validation scoring paths, not epochs, optimization traces or online rating updates; the window selected the models.

figures.title: Held-out scores, including simple baselines
figures.caption:
Log loss uses natural logarithms; Brier is the sum over three classes, not the class-average convention.
Accuracy is argmax classification. Uniform ties choose home; its accuracy is not random-guess expected accuracy.

figures.title: Calibration: probability versus observed frequency
figures.caption:
Ten equal-width probability bins; labels show bin counts n. Empty bins are omitted. Diagonal indicates exact calibration.
95% Wilson binomial intervals are unadjusted for repeated-team/group dependence; no recalibration is fitted to test outcomes.

figures.title: Where the classification errors occur
figures.caption:
Counts, not row-normalized percentages. Rows are actual classes; columns are argmax predictions.
Nonzero draw probabilities do not imply draw picks: the draw column is retained even when every entry is zero.

figures.title: Every match, every outcome probability
figures.caption:
All held-out fixtures, sorted by group, date and match ID. H / D / A = listed home win / draw / listed away win.
Numbers are forecast percentages; orange outlines mark the realized class. Home/away listing is not always venue advantage.

figures.title: Performance varies across tournament groups
figures.caption:
Arithmetic mean log loss within each group; dotted lines show model-wide averages. No shrinkage or group-specific fitting.
Small groups make apparent differences noisy. Group breakdowns are descriptive, not independent validation sets.

figures.title: Apparent advantages carry uncertainty
figures.caption:
Paired log-loss differences; 4,000 resamples, seed 2026, percentile 95% intervals. Negative values favor the first model.
Group resampling keeps each group intact; only 12 clusters. Conditional on fixed models; not team/network robust or evidence of betting edge.

figures.title: The most confident mistakes
figures.caption:
For each model, the eight incorrect argmax predictions with highest confidence; ties use date and match ID.
Labels show actual score. This post-hoc diagnostic does not alter parameters or recalibrate forecasts; high confidence is not certainty.
